title: Basic and molecular genetics
text: Course material for Basic and molecular genetics (5MO104, 15 ECTS, Umeå University). The material follows the course book, Hartwell et al., Genetics: From Genes to Genomes. On top of the genetics, every unit trains you to find information in public databases and to analyse it in R.

title: Basic and molecular genetics
text:
How each unit works
Work through the sidebar from top to bottom. Each unit has:

a lecture (slides, in green);
a quiz (in blue) to check that you understood the concepts;
an exercise, in this order:

By hand: genetics problems on paper.
Explore: an interactive demo (in orange).
Find it: look up real genes, diseases and variants in public databases.
In R: a small analysis or simulation.

title: Basic and molecular genetics
text:
Topics

Part 1: Mendelian genetics. Genes and alleles, Mendel’s laws, probability and the χ² test, extensions to Mendel (dominance, lethality, epistasis, penetrance), and pedigree analysis.
More parts follow the course book: chromosomes and mapping, DNA and mutation, genome analysis, chromosomes in detail, gene regulation and development, and population and complex-trait genetics.

See Canvas for the most up-to-date study instructions.

text:
Unit
A student can…
ELO




Genetics as information
describe DNA → gene → protein → phenotype; distinguish gene, allele, locus, genotype and phenotype; find a gene in NCBI Gene and Ensembl
1, B1


Mendel
predict monohybrid and dihybrid outcomes with Punnett squares and the branch-line method; explain segregation and independent assortment in terms of meiosis; simulate a cross in R
1, 2, B5, B7


Probability & χ²
apply the product and sum rules and the binomial; carry out a χ² goodness-of-fit test by hand and in R and interpret the p-value
3, B4


Extensions to Mendel
recognise incomplete dominance, codominance, multiple alleles, lethal alleles, epistasis, penetrance and expressivity from ratios and descriptions; test which modified ratio fits
1, 3, B1, B4


Pedigree analysis
read pedigrees; decide between autosomal/X-linked and dominant/recessive inheritance; compute carrier and risk probabilities; look up a disease’s inheritance in OMIM
1, 2, B1

title: Install R and the packages you need
text:
1. R and an editor
Install a recent R (4.3 or newer) and RStudio Desktop, or another editor you like.

title: Install R and the packages you need
text:
2. Packages
install.packages("tidyverse")   # dplyr, ggplot2, readr, stringr, tidyr, purrr
That is all the core material needs. Any data an exercise uses can be downloaded from that exercise’s page.
